services.title: AI & Machine Learning Solutions

Our MLOps practice connects data science and operations. We establish reproducible training runs, automated model validation, and drift detection to keep your AI systems robust and cost-effective in production.

Behind the scenes, we develop clean, modular APIs and resilient databases capable of processing high-volume transactions, so your user experience stays smooth and uninterrupted under any load.

services.title: Cloud Services

Security and compliance are built into our design by default, using strict IAM roles, VPC isolation, and end-to-end encryption.
Whether you're migrating legacy servers to the cloud or want serverless computing for event-driven workflows, we build infrastructure sized to your actual budget.

work.title: FixAlert, Maintenance Platform
work.description: A computerized maintenance-management platform with asynchronous reporting, QR-based workflows, and Stripe billing.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: FixAlert needed its reporting and maintenance-tracking workflows rebuilt: database queries were slowing under load, PDF report generation and payments ran synchronously, and the analytics views needed more advanced filtering than the UI supported.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We eliminated N+1 queries and reworked database access patterns to keep the API responsive under heavy load. We moved bulk PDF generation, QR code workflows, and Stripe payments to asynchronous Celery pipelines. On the frontend, we revamped the UI, rebuilt the reporting metric views with React Query, and added nested filtering across analytics, property management, and role-based views.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The API stayed responsive under load with the N+1 fixes in place, and reporting, PDF generation, and payments now run as background jobs instead of blocking the request cycle.

work.title: Landit, Career Platform
work.description: A React and Next.js career-pathing platform used by Fortune 500 companies, with Django APIs, a Looker analytics dashboard, and zero-downtime framework migrations.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: Landit's frontend was running on aging dependencies: Material UI v4, React Router v4, and Formik, all due for migration without disrupting a live platform serving Fortune 500 clients like Pfizer, MetLife, and NBCUniversal. Stakeholders also had no direct visibility into platform metrics.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We executed zero-downtime migrations to Material UI v5 and React Router v5, and moved form handling from Formik to React Hook Form for better performance and maintainability. We also built out the testing infrastructure behind the growing Material UI component library: Storybook for component-level documentation and regression checks, and Jest/Cypress for unit and end-to-end coverage, so new features stopped quietly breaking things that already worked. On the backend, we built and maintained the APIs, developed transactional email workflows with SendGrid, and owned the design and delivery of a Google Looker analytics dashboard.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The migrations shipped with zero downtime, the component library stayed reliable as it grew, and stakeholders gained real-time visibility into key platform metrics through the new Looker dashboard.

work.title: PsychPlus, Telehealth Platform
work.description: A HIPAA-compliant telehealth platform on Django, PostgreSQL, and Kubernetes, with NLP-driven patient insights and real-time clinical data sync.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: PsychPlus needed a telehealth platform that could handle real-time clinical data, patient-provider matching at scale, and strict HIPAA compliance for protected health information as it moves between clinical systems, on top of the NLP and predictive modeling behind its mental-health analytics.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We architected the platform on Django and PostgreSQL on AWS RDS, and used Kubernetes for container orchestration so patient-matching and data services could scale and recover automatically. We optimized patient-provider matching through SQL query tuning and Redis caching, and worked with data engineering to streamline the ETL pipelines behind it. On the AI side, we built NLP and predictive models that turn patient data into personalized care insights and recommendations. We integrated HL7 ADT message processing to keep patient events synchronized across clinical systems, with HIPAA-compliant handling of PHI in transit throughout.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The platform has maintained over 99.9% uptime, with response times holding steady under peak traffic. Clinical data flows securely between systems in real time, personalized insights reach patients through the NLP layer, and compliant PHI handling is built into every layer that touches it.

work.title: Meet Gabbi, AI Conversational Platform
work.description: An AI-powered voice and chat intake platform with fine-tuned language models, a containerized microservices backend, and automated CI/CD.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: Meet Gabbi needed a backend that could keep up with an evolving AI assistant. Conversational products live on frequent model and prompt updates, and every one of those changes is a deployment risk if the infrastructure underneath isn't built for fast, safe releases.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We designed and implemented a microservices backend on Python/Flask, Docker, and AWS ECS, splitting retrieval, inference, and chat handling into services that could scale and deploy independently instead of shipping as one monolith. On the AI side, we layered in fine-tuned language models for natural dialogue and context-aware responses. We set up a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline that automated build, test, and deployment, and worked with product and frontend teams in an Agile setup to turn feature requirements directly into deployable pipelines.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The automated pipeline cut release time by 30%, turning what used to be a manual, risky release process into a repeatable one, with infrastructure changes staying in step with product changes instead of trailing behind them.

work.title: Enterprise API Platform, Monolith-to-Microservices Migration
work.description: A legacy monolith serving millions of daily requests, migrated to Kubernetes-orchestrated microservices on AWS without disrupting live enterprise traffic.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: Legacy monoliths hit a wall as traffic grows: a single deployable application becomes a single point of failure, and every release risks taking the whole platform down. The challenge was migrating a production system already serving enterprise clients to a microservices architecture without disrupting the millions of requests it was already handling daily.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We broke apart the legacy Django/Flask monolith into independently deployable services running on Docker and Kubernetes, removing the single-point-of-failure risk of the old architecture. We re-architected the RESTful API layer for enterprise-scale traffic through service isolation, query optimization, and caching, and layered Jenkins and GitHub Actions CI/CD on top of the new Kubernetes setup.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The migration cut API response times by 40% and downtime by 25%, moving the team from bi-weekly manual releases to daily automated ones while still scaling to serve millions of daily requests.

work.title: Unlock Trader Capital, Algorithmic Trading Platform
work.description: Cloud architecture and a Django/Flask backend for a platform offering automated trading, real-time trade alerts, and professional trade execution for retail traders.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: Trading systems have zero tolerance for infrastructure that's mostly reliable. Latency costs money directly, and downtime during market hours isn't an inconvenience, it's a missed trade. Unlock Trader Capital needed infrastructure that could support algorithmic trading and real-time data analytics without the lag or instability that's fatal in fintech.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We structured the Django/Flask backend and cloud setup around the response-time demands of algorithmic trading, where delays translate directly into missed opportunities, and prioritized infrastructure resilience given the financial stakes of any downtime during active trading windows. We also built out the cloud foundation supporting the real-time data analytics feeding the trading algorithms, not just the trading logic itself.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The platform runs on infrastructure built for the latency and reliability automated trading demands, supporting live algorithmic trading and real-time trade alerts without introducing lag during active market hours.

work.title: KITO, Computer Vision Platform
work.description: Cloud infrastructure for a computer vision platform running deep learning models for image classification, object detection, and visual analytics.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: Computer vision workloads are infrastructure-hungry. Training and running inference on deep learning models needs serious compute, and without the right architecture, costs spiral fast or performance craters under real usage. KITO needed infrastructure that could handle both training and real-time inference without one starving the other.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We built deep learning models for image classification, object detection, and visual analytics, and set up cloud infrastructure sized for both the training and inference sides of that workload. Model serving was structured to scale with demand rather than running fixed, over-provisioned capacity around the clock, balancing performance against the cost overhead compute-heavy CV models tend to introduce.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: Training and real-time inference now run on the same infrastructure without either starving the other, and inference capacity scales with demand instead of sitting over-provisioned.

work.title: Rumi, Frontend CI/CD & Code Quality Infrastructure
work.description: A GitLab CI/CD pipeline and enforced code-quality tooling for Rumi's frontend, alongside architectural refactoring for state-management reliability.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: As frontend codebases grow, quality erodes fast without enforced standards and automated pipelines: inconsistent code, manual deploys, and bugs that slip through because nothing catches them before merge. Rumi's codebase needed infrastructure that enforced quality automatically instead of relying on manual review discipline.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We built out a GitLab CI pipeline to automate build, test, and deployment, and set up ESLint, Prettier, and pre-commit hooks so quality checks ran before code ever reached the pipeline. We wrote unit and integration tests with Vitest to give the pipeline something real to gate on, and refactored the frontend architecture to cut unnecessary re-renders and improve state-management reliability.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: Quality checks now run automatically before every merge instead of depending on manual review, and the release process no longer has manual steps in it.

work.title: Taiga, Open-Source Agile Project Management
work.description: New feature infrastructure, permissions logic, and structured feedback workflows built into Taiga's existing AngularJS and Django architecture.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: Taiga is an established open-source Agile project management tool, so any new feature has to slot into its existing modular architecture without breaking what's already there. Backend endpoints, frontend controllers, and permission logic all had to stay consistent with the existing system instead of being bolted on.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We designed and built the Requestor and Feedback modules across Taiga's AngularJS frontend and Django backend: new models, API endpoints, and reusable directives and controllers within the existing modular structure rather than one-off code that would fragment the codebase. We implemented role-based access control for both features by extending Taiga's existing permission model instead of working around it.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The Requestor and Feedback modules shipped as part of Taiga's existing modular architecture, extending its permission system instead of working around it, without introducing one-off code that would have fragmented the codebase.

work.title: AskImam, Platform Stability & Version Upgrade
work.description: A version upgrade and stability pass on a long-running Islamic Q&A platform founded in 2000, done without disrupting a large, active user base.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: Upgrading a live platform's core dependencies is one of the riskier jobs in production work: done wrong, it breaks existing functionality for real users with no warning. AskImam, founded in 2000, needed a version upgrade and stability pass without taking the platform down or introducing regressions for its established user base.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We upgraded the project to a newer stack version while resolving the major bugs that surfaced along the way, prioritizing stability over a rushed migration. We also updated the Django admin dashboard to make day-to-day platform management more reliable, and integrated Google Analytics to give the team visibility into user engagement.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The upgrade shipped without downtime or regressions for AskImam's active user base, and the team now has real usage data to inform what comes next.

work.title: Wear To Fit, Streetwear E-Commerce Platform
work.description: A Shopify storefront for a Lahore-based streetwear and athleisure brand, built end to end from theme to checkout.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: Wear To Fit needed a store that could go up against international streetwear brands on quality and design without matching their prices. The catalog had to span menswear, womenswear, jewelry, and nutrition products, and it needed to ship nationwide from day one.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We built the Shopify storefront end to end: theme design, the product catalog structure, and checkout. Collections were organized around how people actually shop, New Arrivals, Best Sellers, and category pages like T-Shirts, Trousers, and Summer Tracksuits, instead of one flat product list, and we added WhatsApp chat so customers could reach support directly from the storefront.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The store now ships across Pakistan, from Lahore and Karachi to Islamabad and Peshawar, with a live catalog running into the hundreds of products across menswear, womenswear, jewelry, and nutrition. The site today reports over 12,000 customers served and a 4.8-star average rating.

work.title: HI Legal, Solicitors Website
work.description: A WordPress site for a Newport solicitors firm, covering corporate law, litigation, immigration, and property services.

sections.heading: Challenge
paragraphs: HI Legal needed a site built specifically around a law firm's needs: clear service pages across corporate, litigation, immigration, and property law, a team presence built around its solicitors, and a way to keep clients informed with regularly updated legal news.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: We built the WordPress site end to end: theme, page structure, and content setup across services, team profiles, and a legal news section the firm can publish to directly. Service pages are organized by practice area so visitors can go straight to the kind of legal help they need, and a consultation booking flow sits at the top of the site instead of being buried in a contact page.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The site now covers HI Legal's full range of practice areas for individuals, families, and businesses across England and Wales, with a legal news section the firm keeps current and a consultation booking path built into the homepage.

seo.title: Privacy Policy | Britnova Technologies
seo.description: How Britnova Technologies collects, uses and protects personal information on britnova.net, and your rights under UK data protection law.

privacy.headline: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains how Britnova Technologies collects, uses and protects personal information when you use britnova.net or contact us. It is written to meet the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: The controller of your personal information is Britnova Technology (Private) Limited, a private company limited by shares under Pakistan's Companies Act 2017, incorporated on 21 August 2026 and registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (CRO Lahore) under CUIN 0351933. Its registered office is House # 14, Ghous E Azam Colony, Gulberg 2, Lahore 54660, Punjab, Pakistan.
We are registering with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the UK data protection regulator, and will publish our registration number here once it is issued.
Our UK operations are led by Khaleel Yafa, Chief Executive Officer (UK). People in the UK can contact him about their personal information at contact@britnova.net.

sections.heading: How to contact us about your data
paragraphs: Email contact@britnova.net and we will respond to any request about your personal information.
We have not appointed a Data Protection Officer, because the UK GDPR does not require one for our activities.

sections.heading: What we collect, why, and our lawful basis
paragraphs: We only collect what we need. Please do not include sensitive information (such as health details) in messages to us.
items: Contact form (your name, email address, project type and message). We use it to reply to your enquiry and to discuss possible work with you. Lawful basis: our legitimate interest in answering business enquiries, or, if you ask us for a proposal or quote, steps you have asked us to take before entering into a contract.

Messages you send us directly, including email, WhatsApp, phone calls and Calendly bookings. We use them to reply and to manage our work with you. Lawful basis: our legitimate interest in answering and managing business enquiries, or the steps needed to enter into or carry out a contract with you.

Website analytics: the page visited, the page you came from, the page title, your screen size and browser language, plus general device and location information derived from the request. We use this in aggregate to understand how the site is used, and it is on unless you turn it off with the Analytics switch in the footer or your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal. Lawful basis: our legitimate interest in improving the website.
Technical data our hosting provider handles to deliver and secure the site, such as your IP address and request details. Lawful basis: our legitimate interest in running a secure website.

sections.heading: Who we share it with
paragraphs: We use trusted providers to run the site and our business. They act on our instructions as processors:
items: Resend, which delivers contact-form messages to us by email.
Netlify, which hosts the website and runs the function that handles the contact form.
Umami, which provides website analytics (you can turn this off in the footer).
Hostinger, which provides our email, including the contact@britnova.net mailbox.
Calendly, which handles meeting bookings if you book a call with us.
Professional advisers, such as accountants or lawyers, only where we need their help.
closing: We do not sell your personal information.

sections.heading: Transfers outside the UK
paragraphs: Some of the providers above are based in, or process information in, the United States, and our team works from the UK, Pakistan and Canada.

The UK has adequacy regulations covering Canada (for organisations subject to Canada's PIPEDA) and US organisations certified under the UK Extension to the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, but not Pakistan. We are confirming with our adviser which safeguards UK law requires for the transfers we make, and will describe them here.
You can ask us about this at any time.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Enquiries that do not lead to work: 12 months after our last contact, then we delete them. Client records: for the length of our work together, and afterwards for as long as Pakistani tax and company law requires us to keep business records. Website analytics: kept as overall statistics, which do not include your name or contact details.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: Under UK data protection law you have the right to:
items: be told how your information is used (this policy);
access the personal information we hold about you;
have inaccurate information corrected;
have your information erased in certain circumstances;
restrict how we use it in certain circumstances;
receive your information in a portable format where it applies;
turn analytics off at any time with the Analytics switch in the footer of every page.
closing: You also have the right to object to our use of your information where we rely on legitimate interests. Tell us and we will stop unless we can show a compelling reason to continue.
To use any of these rights, email us. We will normally respond within one month. We do not use automated decision-making or profiling on this website.

sections.heading: Complaints
paragraphs: We would like the chance to put things right first, so please contact us. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office, the UK data protection regulator, on 0303 123 1113.

links.label: Make a complaint to the ICO

sections.heading: Cookies and similar technologies
paragraphs: Our Cookie Policy lists exactly what this website stores on your device and how to change your choices.

sections.heading: Other websites
paragraphs: This website links to services such as LinkedIn, WhatsApp and Calendly. They have their own privacy policies and we are not responsible for them.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We will update this page if how we use personal information changes, and show the date at the top.

seo.title: Cookie Policy | Britnova Technologies
seo.description: What britnova.net stores on your device, why, and how to turn analytics off.

cookies.headline: Cookie Policy
cookies.intro: This website does not set cookies and does not use advertising or tracking, so there is no cookie banner. It stores two small items in your browser's local storage, and runs privacy-focused analytics that you can switch off at any time. UK law (PECR) treats local storage in the same way as cookies, so we list everything here.

sections.heading: What this website stores
items: Your theme (britnova-theme). Saved only if you use the light/dark switch, so the site opens how you left it. It changes only how the site looks. You can clear it by clearing this site's data in your browser.
Analytics off switch (umami.disabled). Saved only if you turn analytics off, so it stays off on your next visit.

sections.heading: Analytics
paragraphs: We use Umami, a privacy-focused analytics service, to see overall visit numbers and which pages are useful. Its script sets no cookies and stores nothing else on your device. It sends the page address, the page you came from, the page title, your screen size and your browser language to Umami. We use the results as overall statistics. We do not use them for advertising or to build profiles of individual visitors.
UK law allows analytics like this without asking first, as long as we tell you clearly what we do and make it easy to object. This page is that information, and the switch below is the way to object.

sections.heading: Turn analytics off or on
paragraphs: Use the Analytics switch here or in the footer of any page. Turning it off is as easy as turning it on, and nothing is sent to Umami while it is off.
If your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as turned off until you switch it on.

sections.heading: Third-party links
paragraphs: Links to LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Calendly and other sites take you to services that may set their own cookies. We do not control them, so please read their policies.

sections.heading: Server information
paragraphs: Our hosting provider receives technical details such as your IP address each time a page is requested, which is how any website works. This is described in our Privacy Policy.

seo.title: Accessibility Statement | Britnova Technologies
seo.description: How accessible britnova.net is, what we tested, the known issues, and how to contact us about accessibility.

accessibility.headline: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.updated: First published: 14 October 2026. Last reviewed: 14 October 2026
accessibility.intro: This statement applies to britnova.net. We want everyone to be able to use this website, including people who use screen readers, keyboards, magnification or other assistive technology.

sections.heading: Our standard
paragraphs: We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA. We are a private company and are not covered by the Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) Accessibility Regulations 2018, but we follow the same standard and the structure of the GOV.UK model statement so that public sector clients can see where we stand.

sections.heading: Compliance status
paragraphs: This website is partially compliant with WCAG 2.2 AA. We have tested it ourselves and found no failures of the AA criteria that we tested, but we have not yet had an independent audit or testing with screen reader users, so we cannot claim full compliance. The limits of our testing are listed below.

sections.heading: What you can do
items: Use the whole site with a keyboard. A 'Skip to main content' link is the first item you reach.
Zoom in to 400% (or use a 320 pixel wide window) without scrolling sideways.
Choose a light or dark theme with the switch on every page.
Pause the moving technology logos using the 'Pause motion' button. Animations also stop automatically if your device is set to reduce motion.

sections.heading: Known limitations
items: We have not yet tested with screen readers such as NVDA, JAWS or VoiceOver.
We have not had an independent accessibility audit.
Links to other services, such as Calendly, LinkedIn and WhatsApp, open sites we do not control.
Images of our case studies have text descriptions, but we have not independently checked each one for quality.

sections.heading: Feedback and contact
paragraphs: If you find a barrier, or need information in another format, email contact@britnova.net. We will reply within 5 working days and tell you what we can do.

sections.heading: If you are not happy with our response
paragraphs: If you are not satisfied with how we respond, you can contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service (EASS), which gives advice on discrimination and equality in England, Scotland and Wales.

sections.heading: How we tested
paragraphs: Tested by our own team on 13 October 2026 on the home, services, work, case study, about, contact, privacy, cookie and accessibility pages, in light and dark themes.
items: Automated: axe-core 4.14.0 against the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA rules plus best-practice rules, and a Lighthouse accessibility audit.
Manual: keyboard-only navigation and visible focus, colour contrast of text over the gradient background, size and spacing of clickable targets, and reflow at 320 pixels wide.

sections.heading: How often we review this
paragraphs: We will review this statement at least once a year and whenever we make a major change to the website.
